subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the value of x if the determinant with rows (x−2, 2x−3, 3x−4), (x−4, 2x−9, 3x−16) and (x−8, 2x−27, 3x−64) is 0.

mark_split.label: Subtract R₁ from R₂ and R₃

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.40, chapter 5 MATRICES, Short Answer question 8. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1+1+1 shape gives one mark each to the row subtractions, the common factors, the expansion, and solving for x. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B runs Q11 to Q18 at 4 marks each, answer any 6 of 8, under the 2026-27 pattern; Matrices carries a Section B slot and also appears in Section C. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find x here — name each row operation in order.

steps.label: Subtract R₁ from R₂ and R₃
steps.margin_note: First mark. Every entry carries an x, so subtracting one row from another cancels all of them. Two rows then hold plain numbers and the question becomes easy.
steps.memory_tip: Every entry carries an x, so row subtraction cancels the x from two whole rows.
lines: Apply R₂ → R₂ − R₁ and R₃ → R₃ − R₁.
The x terms cancel in both rows:

recall.must_convey: That R₂ → R₂ − R₁ and R₃ → R₃ − R₁ are applied, and that x cancels in those two rows.
accept: subtract the first row from the second and from the third
apply R two minus R one and R three minus R one
the x terms cancel and the last two rows become plain numbers
R two minus R one, R three minus R one cheste x poddi
row subtraction clears x from the bottom two rows

steps.why: Subtracting one row from another does not change the value of a determinant, so this is free — and it removes x from six of the nine entries.
common_mistakes: Expanding the determinant with x still in all nine entries.
Subtracting in the wrong direction, so the signs of both new rows come out reversed.

steps.label: Take out the common factors
steps.margin_note: Second mark. −2 comes out of R₂ and −6 out of R₃, so a factor 12 sits outside. Then one more subtraction puts a zero in R₃.
steps.memory_tip: −2 out of R₂ and −6 out of R₃ leaves the clean factor 12 outside.
lines: Take −2 out of R₂ and −6 out of R₃:

recall.must_convey: That −2 and −6 are taken out, giving 12 outside, and that R₃ → R₃ − R₂ creates a zero.
accept: take minus two out of the second row and minus six out of the third
minus two into minus six is twelve so twelve comes outside
then subtract the second row from the third to make a zero
minus two, minus six common teesthe twelve bayata vasthundi
pull the common factors out and reduce the last row

steps.why: A factor taken out of a row multiplies the determinant outside. Two negative factors give (−2)(−6) = 12, a positive number, so no sign is lost.
common_mistakes: Taking −2 and −6 out and writing −12 instead of 12.
Taking the factor out of one entry of the row instead of the whole row.

steps.label: Expand to 12(x − 4)
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Expand along R₁ with the + − + sign pattern. The constant terms −12, +12 and −4 leave −4, and the x terms leave a single x.
steps.memory_tip: The three minors are 6, 4 and 1, so the whole determinant collapses to 12(x − 4).

recall.must_convey: That expanding along R₁ with the + − + signs gives Δ = 12(x − 4).
accept: expand along the first row using plus minus plus
the minors are six, four and one so it becomes twelve into x minus four
six x minus twelve minus eight x plus twelve plus three x minus four is x minus four
first row expand cheste twelve into x minus four vasthundi
delta equals twelve times x minus four

steps.why: Every entry outside R₁ is now a small whole number, so the three minors are easy and the answer comes out as one bracket in x.
common_mistakes: Using + + + instead of the + − + sign pattern along the row.

steps.label: Solve for x
steps.margin_note: Last mark. 12 is never zero, so only the bracket can vanish. Substituting x = 4 gives the rows (2, 5, 8), (0, −1, −4) and (−4, −19, −52), whose determinant is 0 — the answer checks.
steps.memory_tip: 12 can never be zero, so only the bracket x − 4 can make the determinant vanish.

recall.must_convey: That 12(x − 4) = 0 forces x = 4, because 12 is not zero.
accept: twelve is not zero so x minus four must be zero
x equals four
set the bracket to zero and get x is four
twelve zero kaadu kabatti x minus four zero avvali
the determinant is zero only when x is four

steps.why: A product is zero only when one of its factors is zero. The constant factor 12 cannot be zero, so the bracket carries the whole equation.
common_mistakes: Dividing by (x − 4) and losing the solution.
Reporting x = 12 or x = −4 by reading the wrong number out of the bracket.
